headline: Exploit code caught up with the week's biggest server flaws as attackers probed Java4Shell, proof-of-concept exploits for the decade-old nginx2root bugs went public, and intruders took over clustered Cisco Expressway systems days after a researcher published working code.

emerging_trends.text: Attackers treat a published proof of concept as a starting gun: exploit traffic reached Java4Shell, the nginx2root HTTP/2 bugs, and clustered Cisco Expressway devices within days of the code going public.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Cisco Expressway and Apache Axis Enter Active Exploitation

emerging_trends.text: Artex, the open-source AI penetration-testing framework, has become the entry-level weapon for newcomers who type a prompt instead of writing an exploit, while the same agent plumbing runs unmonitored inside companies on employees' own credentials.
emerging_trends.topic_title: AI Agents Run on Their Builders' Credentials

emerging_trends.text: This week's victims sit downstream of a vendor rather than at the point of attack, with Wellington IT exposing member records at 50 credit unions and N-able losing a server inside its hosted email security cloud.
emerging_trends.topic_title: N-able Mail Cloud and Wellington IT Breaches Spread

topics.title: nginx2root Exploits Go Public as Splunk Patches 140 Bugs
topics.latest_developments: F5 patched five nginx2root vulnerabilities that let remote, unauthenticated attackers run arbitrary code, and proof-of-concept exploits for them reached the public, with researchers chaining two of the bugs to a Linux kernel flaw to take root; Splunk fixed nearly 140 flaws across three core products, among them authentication bypass, remote code execution, and privilege escalation; and SonicWall told customers in a Wednesday advisory to replace every Gen 6 and Gen 6.5 appliance and pull it off the internet edge, because SonicOS 6.x now receives no firmware or security updates regardless of severity.
topics.summary: The nginx2root bugs have sat in NGINX's open-source HTTP/2 code since version 1.9.5 shipped on September 22, 2015, and F5 fixed them in 1.31.9 and 1.30.7. Any internet-facing NGINX with HTTP/2 enabled, Splunk deployment, or SonicWall Gen 6 firewall needs action this week.

sources.title: F5 Patches Critical NGINX2Root Flaws as PoC Exploits Go Public
Critical NGINX 'NGINX2Root' bugs let attackers hijack servers
Splunk Patches Nearly 140 Flaws Across Three Core Products

topics.title: Cisco Expressway and Apache Axis Enter Active Exploitation
topics.latest_developments: Attackers exploited a Cisco Expressway vulnerability soon after a proof of concept went out, hacking clustered Expressway devices at a Russian organization and staging tooling for lateral movement; the Apache Software Foundation warned of attacks on Roller through CVE-2026-129448, the unauthenticated XML-RPC deserialization bug rated 9.8, while a separate Apache Axis flaw now serves as the way into Confluence Data Center; CISA tied its four newest Known Exploited Vulnerabilities entries, covering Synology DiskStation Manager, BerriAI LiteLLM, Apache Axis, and Vanderbilt University's Research Electronic Data Capture platform, to ransomware, cryptomining, and LLMjacking, and ordered federal civilian agencies to fix the Perforce Puppet Enterprise flaw CVE-2026-115731; Drupal patched a critical remote code execution bug and told site owners to expect exploits fast.
topics.summary: Five widely deployed products—Cisco Expressway, Apache Roller, Apache Axis, Puppet Enterprise, and Drupal—now carry unauthenticated paths to code execution with attacks already running. Patch the internet-facing ones first and treat the Puppet server as a route to every endpoint it configures.

sources.title: Hackers Exploit Cisco Expressway Vulnerability Soon After PoC Release
Critical Apache Roller, Axis Vulnerabilities Exploited in Attacks

topics.title: PHP, Ruby, and Databases Ship Code-Execution Fixes
topics.latest_developments: PHP scheduled releases for November 19, 2026 between 2 and 2:30 p.m. UTC to close CVE-2026-115560, a remote code execution flaw in session upload progress that surfaced two days after the PHP2Shell patches landed and reaches every supported version; Ruby fixed seven memory-safety bugs in its regular expression engine and string case-conversion code, and its maintainers say proof-of-concept exploits run code through five of them; and a researcher published working exploits that carry a low-privilege database account into code execution on PostgreSQL, MySQL, and ClickHouse servers, plus a separate Oracle chain.
topics.summary: Three of the most widely deployed back-end runtimes now carry fresh unauthenticated or low-privilege paths to the operating system account under the service. Upgrade PHP and Ruby as the releases land, and audit which database accounts can create objects or call engine functions.

sources.title: PHP Readies Critical Security Updates to Patch Another RCE Flaw

topics.title: AI Agents Run on Their Builders' Credentials
topics.latest_developments: Nudge Security, drawing on telemetry from its customers' environments, found that the AI agents employees assemble inside project trackers, CRMs, and automation tools run on the credentials of whoever built them and inherit that person's access to company data, with no one monitoring how the agents spend it; Wired documented Artex, the open-source AI penetration-testing framework, as the point-and-shoot tool newcomers now use to scan and attack targets through chatbot prompts; Microsoft moved its Perception agentic security platform out of preview, making four blue team agents and the Recon Agent generally available; and Palo Alto Networks agreed to buy Applied Compute, which post-trains and runs open-weight models, for $4.5 billion in stock.
topics.summary: Employee-built agents carry human entitlements into automated workflows while attackers drive the same agent frameworks offensively. Inventory which agents run in your environment, whose identity each one uses, and what systems it can reach.

sources.title: AI agents inherit employee access, and nobody's watching how they use it

topics.title: N-able Mail Cloud and Wellington IT Breaches Spread
topics.latest_developments: NVIDIA said it has found no indication that anyone compromised its systems after the Gentlemen ransomware crew listed the chipmaker on its dark web leak site; N-able disclosed on Wednesday, November 18, 2026 that unknown attackers reached a server in its Mail Assure and Spam Experts Hosted Cloud, and the company disabled management interfaces and APIs across three regions while its investigation continues; a reported attack on Wellington IT exposed sensitive member information at 50 credit unions, most of them in Ireland; and Wired reported that two vulnerabilities in CreditNirvana, the AI debt collection platform, left 6.6 million accounts and 315,000 call recordings open, along with emails, texts, and credit reports.
topics.summary: Four victims this week sit downstream of a provider: a hosted email security cloud, a credit union software vendor, a ransomware leak-site listing, and a debt collection platform holding financial records. Customers of each should force credential rotation and review what access the provider holds.

sources.title: Hackers Breach N-able Cloud Server, Disrupting Email Security Management Across 3 Regions

topics.title: Washington Targets Scam Payments and a Palantir Spy
topics.latest_developments: The Homeland Security Task Force opened the Threat Disruption Center inside its National Coordination Center in Fairfax, Virginia, giving investigators shared tooling to sort victim complaints, map the criminal groups behind them, and stop victims' payments before the money leaves for foreign scam, cybercrime, and sextortion networks; Coinbase blocked $4.7 million in cryptocurrency transfers to a fake giveaway that ran an AI-generated deepfake of Elon Musk during a Tesla livestream more than 500,000 people watched; federal prosecutors charged Igor Andreevich D'iu, a Russian national recruited through Telegram, with acting as a Moscow agent in a surveillance campaign against employees of a defense technology company The Record understands to be Palantir Technologies; and a federal bankruptcy judge cleared Google to take the data of the defunct Spirit Airlines for $10 million, with protections attached, for use in AI projects.
topics.summary: The United States is attacking fraud at the payment layer while prosecuting human-intelligence collection against defense contractor staff. Finance and insider-threat teams gain a new federal contact point for both.

topics.title: Java4Shell Draws Live Exploit Attempts
topics.latest_developments: GreyNoise, watchTowr, and Cloudflare each reported probing and exploit attempts against CVE-2026-114938, and Cisco, Elastic, Red Hat, and Siemens published advisories spelling out which of their products carry the vulnerable runtime; Dark Reading reported that researchers found the flaw using AI.
topics.summary: Java4Shell is a memory corruption bug in the Base64 decoder of the x86-64 HotSpot Java Virtual Machine that hands an attacker who never logs in remote code execution on Jenkins, Atlassian Jira, Confluence, and Keycloak. Any host running Java 17.0.6 or later on an Intel or AMD processor with AVX-512 VBMI needs the patch now.

sources.title: Java4Shell Exploitation Attempts Begin as Vendors Rush Out Advisories
Java4Shell Flaw Threatens Global Enterprises, Java Application Ecosystem

topics.title: Ukraine Arrests a Fake IT Support Ransomware Crew
topics.latest_developments: Ukraine's National Police described how the four suspects worked: they studied each target, then telephoned employees posing as IT support staff to talk their way into corporate networks, and the case ran more than two years with the FBI; The Record identified oil and healthcare companies in the United States among the 28 victims that paid more than $40.5 million.
topics.summary: Ukrainian authorities detained four members of an international ransomware operation that opened its intrusions with voice phishing rather than malware. Help desks and their callers need verification steps that survive a convincing phone call.

sources.title: Ukraine exposes ransomware network extorting US oil, healthcare firms

topics.title: ICE Pays AT&T to Mine Call Records
topics.latest_developments: An internal Immigration and Customs Enforcement document that 404 Media obtained shows the agency paying AT&T for raw data and analytical services under the Hemisphere program, and privacy experts and members of Congress call the arrangement a mass surveillance effort that may touch trillions of phone records.
topics.summary: Hemisphere gives federal investigators searchable access to AT&T call detail records, including calls that merely cross AT&T's network. Anyone whose threat model includes United States law enforcement demands should assume telephone metadata sits inside a commercial analytics service.

sources.title: ICE Is Paying AT&T to Dig Through a Mountain of Call Records

topics.title: Flash Chip Attack Breaks TPM Lockout
topics.latest_developments: Researchers at Technische Universität Berlin showed that anyone who opens the case of an AMD-based PC, and of some Intel PCs, can reset the TPM lockout that throttles PIN guessing, and in lab tests they recovered a four-digit Windows Hello PIN on an AMD laptop and a six-digit BitLocker PIN on an Intel laptop in days.
topics.summary: Short Windows Hello and BitLocker PINs rely on the TPM refusing repeated guesses, and physical access to the flash chip removes that limit. Organizations issuing laptops should require long PINs or pre-boot passphrases and treat a lost machine as a machine an attacker can open.

sources.title: New Attack Bypasses TPM Lockout to Crack Windows Hello and BitLocker PINs in Days, Not Years

business_politics.title: Germany Puts Its Cyber Threat Level at Critical
business_politics.latest_developments: Germany's security authorities reported an artificial-intelligence-driven surge in hacking attempts and rated the national threat level critical, the Financial Times reported Thursday, November 19.
business_politics.summary: New artificial-intelligence tools let attackers find and exploit software flaws far faster, and the German assessment lands a week after outages knocked out systems at Microsoft, JPMorgan Chase, and other large companies. The Economist traces those American failures to frenzied patching and cyber-attack preparation that manufacture fragility of their own, which puts operational risk at banks and cloud providers in the same frame as the attackers.

sources.title: Germany reveals AI-driven surge in cyber attacks
What is causing America's recent outages

business_politics.title: Anthropic Debuts on the Nasdaq
business_politics.latest_developments: Anthropic's Nasdaq debut Thursday, November 19, raised $81.3 billion, the largest initial public offering on record, Treasury yields rose as the listing rekindled risk appetite on Wall Street, and the Wall Street Journal reported that a majority of the lab's more than 5,000 employees stand to become millionaires.
business_politics.summary: Anthropic, the San Francisco maker of the Claude chatbot, sold stock at a $1.5 trillion valuation and becomes the first artificial-intelligence lab to trade publicly. The opening prints give investors their clearest read on appetite for the AI build-out after weeks of selling in Nvidia and data-center shares.

business_politics.title: Trump, Xi, and Putin Hold the First Trilateral Summit
business_politics.latest_developments: The three leaders closed the Shenzhen summit Thursday, November 19, with a joint denunciation of nuclear war and a show of unity on energy security, and they reached no major breakthrough.
business_politics.summary: Trump, Xi Jinping, and Vladimir Putin met in the southern Chinese city during the week of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum, the first meeting ever to put the American, Chinese, and Russian heads of state at one table, and Trump told the room, "We are really making history." Germany hosted 40 delegations in Berlin the same day to back Kyiv and blunt the summit's Yalta 2.0 optics, and the Wall Street Journal argues Trump's leverage abroad is contracting even as he convenes the meeting.

business_politics.title: A Houthi Strike Hits the Saudi Wealth Fund's Tower
business_politics.latest_developments: The Financial Times reported Thursday, November 19, that a week of tit-for-tat strikes between Iran and the United States has carried the two countries toward full-scale confrontation, and The Economist concluded the same day that neither side holds the means to end the war.
business_politics.summary: A Houthi air strike damaged several floors of Riyadh's tallest building Thursday, November 19, the 80-story tower that houses Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund, the kingdom's sovereign wealth fund and one of the world's largest state investors. Crude edged higher the same morning as traders weighed continuing threats to Middle Eastern oil shipments.

business_politics.title: TSMC and Samsung Halt Some China Shipments
business_politics.latest_developments: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company and Samsung Electronics suspended some chip shipments to Chinese customers, the Financial Times reported Thursday, November 19, days after the Commerce Department imposed its new export controls.
business_politics.summary: The two largest contract chipmakers supply processors that go into Chinese phones, servers, and cars, so a sustained halt starves Chinese technology firms of advanced silicon. Alibaba, which reported a sharp earnings rebound Thursday on improving artificial-intelligence profitability, named tighter scrutiny of chip exports to China as a fresh risk to that growth engine.

business.title: Viatris Closes Its $1.65 Billion Pacira Deal
business.latest_developments: Viatris completed its acquisition of Pacira BioSciences in a deal valued at $1.65 billion, the company announced Tuesday, November 17, and WPXI reported Thursday, November 19.
business.summary: Viatris, the Canonsburg drugmaker formed in 2020 from Mylan and the Upjohn business of Pfizer, ranks among the largest public companies based in Western Pennsylvania. Pacira develops pain medications, and the purchase pushes Viatris further beyond generics into branded treatment.

sources.title: Viatris completes $1.6B acquisition

business.title: Achieva Names Court Hower Chief Executive
business.latest_developments: Achieva named Court Hower president and chief executive effective December 14, the organization announced November 17, WPXI reported Thursday, November 19.
business.summary: Achieva runs a $57 million operation providing services, family supports, employment programs, and advocacy for people with disabilities across the Pittsburgh region. Hower inherits one of the larger human-services employers in Allegheny County.

sources.title: Achieva names new CEO to lead $57M organization

business.title: U.S. Steel and the Steelworkers Reach a Tentative Contract
business.latest_developments: The United Steelworkers announced a tentative agreement with U.S. Steel Thursday morning, November 19, covering more than 10,000 workers at 13 facilities.
business.summary: The proposed deal commits $4.5 billion in capital investment at union-represented sites of U.S. Steel, the Pittsburgh company Nippon Steel acquired in 2025, and the Pittsburgh-based United Steelworkers negotiated it for mills that anchor employment across Western Pennsylvania. The capital pledge determines which plants get modernized and which workers keep their jobs.

sources.title: United Steelworkers reach tentative agreement with US Steel on new contract

business.title: AAA Sees Thanksgiving Travel Slip
business.latest_developments: AAA forecast that fewer people will drive or fly for Thanksgiving this year, WTAE reported Thursday, November 19, the first decline in three years, while cruise, bus, and train bookings climb.
business.summary: The forecast covers the holiday week leading to Thanksgiving on Thursday, November 26, 2026, and sets the volume expectations for Pittsburgh International Airport, the Pennsylvania Turnpike, and Amtrak service through the region. Airlines and hotels price the holiday off these projections, and the shift toward rail and bus travel follows a month of airline disruption.

sources.title: Thanksgiving travel dips for the first time in three years

around_town.title: Shaler Area Locks Up Teachers Through 2031-32
around_town.latest_developments: TribLive reported Wednesday night, November 18, that the Shaler Area School District and its teachers signed an early-bird contract that keeps the staff under agreement through the 2031-32 school year.
around_town.summary: The deal settles pay and terms six years out for teachers in the northern Allegheny County district, which enrolls students from Shaler, Etna, Millvale, and Reserve Township. Districts across the county are fighting over expired contracts, and Shaler Area now takes its labor calendar off the table until 2032.

sources.title: Early-bird contract keeps Shaler Area teachers under contract through 2031-32 school year

around_town.title: Gilpin Township Orders Water Conservation
around_town.latest_developments: The Gilpin Township Municipal Authority imposed a mandatory water conservation notice across its entire service area Wednesday night, November 18, and blamed insufficient water pressure coming from the Municipal Authority of Westmoreland County.
around_town.summary: Gilpin sits in Armstrong County along the Allegheny River and buys its water through the Westmoreland County system. The order takes effect immediately for every customer the township authority serves.

around_town.title: Frosty Mornings, Mild Afternoons
around_town.latest_developments: Widespread frost and river-valley fog opened Thursday, November 19, around Pittsburgh under clear skies and light winds, and KDKA, WPXI, and WTAE each carry sunshine and mild, dry weather across Western Pennsylvania into the weekend.
around_town.summary: The dry stretch covers the downtown holiday market, which opens Friday, November 20, and Light Up Night on Saturday, November 21. Temperatures run above normal through the weekend with no rain in the forecast.

around_town.title: Charleroi Police Board Tables the ICE Agreement
around_town.latest_developments: The Charleroi Regional Police board voted Wednesday night, November 18, to table a proposed 287(g) agreement with Immigration and Customs Enforcement after residents, business owners, and community leaders filled the meeting room to oppose it.
around_town.summary: The agreement would let Charleroi Regional Police officers act as federal immigration enforcement agents in the Washington County borough, where the Haitian population has thinned since federal Temporary Protected Status ended. Speakers told the board the deal would spread fear and cost borough businesses customers they have already begun to lose.

around_town.title: Sto-Rox Teachers Authorize a Strike
around_town.latest_developments: WTAE reported Thursday, November 19, that the Sto-Rox Education Association has now worked 142 days under an expired contract, a day after members voted with full support to authorize a strike, and union officials said they will hold off on a walkout for now.
around_town.summary: The Sto-Rox School District, which serves McKees Rocks and Stowe Township in Allegheny County, has yet to settle terms with its teachers, and the union had not taken a strike authorization vote in decades. The vote hands union leadership the power to call a walkout whenever it judges one necessary, which would idle classes for the district's students.

around_town.title: Pittsburgh's $43 Million in No-Bid Contracts
around_town.latest_developments: PublicSource published an analysis Thursday, November 19, finding the City of Pittsburgh has issued roughly $43 million in contracts since 2020 without a competitive process.
around_town.summary: The sum amounts to a small fraction of total city spending, and it has drawn intense scrutiny of how Pittsburgh picks vendors. The explainer walks through the rules that let the city skip bidding and where the money went.

events.title: The Holiday Market Opens Friday in Market Square
events.latest_developments: KDKA reported Thursday, November 19, that Pittsburgh's holiday market opens Friday, November 20, in Market Square, with Light Up Night following Saturday, November 21.
events.summary: Vendors in the wooden chalets downtown told KDKA they are ready for the holiday shopping season to start, and Light Up Night brings the crowds, skaters, and families that merchants around the square count on. The market runs in Market Square through the shopping season.

events.latest_developments: NEXTpittsburgh published its weekend guide covering Thursday, November 19, through Sunday, November 22, with more than 13 things to do, led by Light Up Night, Phipps Conservatory's Holiday Magic, and a cryptid film festival.

around_teams.title: Rodgers Takes Questions Before Philadelphia
around_teams.latest_developments: The Steelers posted video Thursday morning, November 19, of Aaron Rodgers's Wednesday news conference, November 18, his first media session of the week.
around_teams.summary: Rodgers, the Steelers quarterback, spoke three days after the loss at Cincinnati that put the passing game under scrutiny, and Pittsburgh plays the Philadelphia Eagles Sunday, November 22, at 1 p.m. Eastern on CBS. Matt Williamson and Wes Uhler opened the same week's SNR Drive on the Eagles matchup.

sources.title: Aaron Rodgers Press Conference (November 18) | Pittsburgh Steelers

team_usa.title: Arena Blasts the U.S. Coaching Search
team_usa.latest_developments: Bruce Arena said U.S. Soccer does not "have a clue" how to replace Mauricio Pochettino, ESPN reported Thursday, November 19.
team_usa.summary: Arena, who coached the United States men's national team at the 2002 and 2006 World Cups and now manages the San Jose Earthquakes, took aim at the federation two days after Pochettino left for Manchester United. Steve Cherundolo runs the December camp on an interim basis while U.S. Soccer, with women's coach Emma Hayes helping assess candidates, searches for a permanent hire ahead of the 2030 cycle.

team_usa.title: Sanchez Wins the NWSL MVP Award
team_usa.latest_developments: The National Women's Soccer League named Ashley Sanchez its 2026 Most Valuable Player Wednesday, November 18, placing her ahead of Trinity Rodman in the voting.
team_usa.summary: Sanchez, the North Carolina Courage forward and a United States international, tied the league record with 20 goals this season. The award caps a year that puts her in the conversation for Emma Hayes's World Cup qualifying squads.

sources.title: Courage striker Sanchez beats out Rodman, Wilson for NWSL MVP award

team_usa.title: The NWSL Final Arrives With Old Problems
team_usa.latest_developments: ESPN reported Thursday, November 19, that record revenue has failed to solve the National Women's Soccer League's stadium and scheduling problems as the Kansas City Current and the Washington Spirit prepare to meet in Saturday's championship, November 21.
team_usa.summary: Venue conflicts pushed both semifinals into unsuitable buildings last weekend, and Gotham FC forward Midge Purce called the 5,000-seat Icahn Stadium assignment inexcusable. The final pairs Kansas City against a Washington side chasing its third straight title with Trinity Rodman leading the attack.
